paper.title_en: C-infinity Compact-Support Wormholes with Exact Schwarzschild Exterior in Trace-Coupled Gravity
paper.abstract_en: We construct static, spherically symmetric wormholes in trace-coupled gravity with $f(R,T)=R+λT^2$. Smooth deformations of Schwarzschild vanish to all orders outside a finite core, producing an exact Schwarzschild exterior without a thin shell. Under two explicitly assumed anisotropic-fluid closures, the matter reconstruction reduces to a cubic equation for $χ=λT/(4π)$. The vacuum boundary selects a locally unique root; its simple continuation must remain separate from the singular inversion surface. We distinguish root folds from vanishing $1+χ$ and terminate numerical continuation when the selected root coalesces. Regular examples have either positive or negative throat density. On every regular branch the physical radial null energy condition fails at the throat; for the undeformed-redshift family it fails throughout the open core. The nonvacuum sector has finite support, whereas the exterior retains the Schwarzschild Weyl field and mass $M$. Reproducible phase maps, convergence tests, and high-precision tail checks support these conditional existence results. No dynamical stability or microphysical matter model is asserted.
